alex_mason: Heads-up — noticed ~15-20% regression on p95 for short-chat traffic after last envoy + rust-shim push (commit ab12c). Trying to triage host-side overhead (tokenization + parse + streaming).
priya_k: Any flamegraph / perf samples? short-chat workloads are sensitive to host overhead. :eyes: 
alex_mason: Pasted top of collapsed flamegraph from 1k samples (short requests):
```
parse_request                            37%
tokenize_rust_shim                       25%
writev_syscall                           15%
grpc_serialize                           10%
kernel_selector_idle                      3%
other                                    10%
```
priya_k: tokenize_rust_shim at 25% is surprising — did we change boundary handling? mattw recently touched streaming chunker.
mattw: I changed chunk framing to prefer smaller frames for gRPC interop (safer for marginal clients). That increases syscall count for small messages. Could be writev thrash.
sara_d: Also saw KV cache hit rate drop on short prefixes yesterday — priya, alex any correlation?
alex_mason: yes — kv hit rate dropped from 98% -> 86% for 0-64 token prefixes in the same window. I think tokenization is producing different token boundary splits (extra leading whitespace tokens) which change cache keys.
priya_k: Do we have a repro curl + payload to iterate?
alex_mason: Minimal repro:
```
curl -sv -X POST https://ingress.internal/v1/generate \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"prompt":"hi","max_tokens":16,"stream":true}'
```
Then capture host-side trace with `perf record -g` while running 200rps.
mattw: Quick wins: 1) coalesce writes with MSG_MORE/vec writev to reduce syscalls 2) revert framing tweak to 1k default for canary 3) reuse token buffers across requests to reduce allocs.
sara_d: On the KV side we should normalize tokenization output used as cache key (trim leading whitespace token) so minor boundary diffs don't evict. Also add a small prefix hash tolerance (fingerprint first N tokens canonicalized).
priya_k: I instrumented syscall breakdown — write/open/close show heavy writev spikes aligned with tokenization peak. If writev latency reduced we get ~10% p95 back (est).
perf-bot: Canary canary-17 rolled back at 4976543275 due to p95 > SLO for short-chat.
alex_mason: Proposed patch list:
- ingress: enable MSG_MORE in rust-shim write path (matt)
- runtime: add token buffer pool BytesMut reuse (sara)
- routing: add cache-key normalization for prefix hits (priya)
- rollback: revert framing size change for canary until we validate.
Can we pair on a quick patch for MSG_MORE? I can PR today.
mattw: I'll prototype MSG_MORE + writev batching this afternoon, also test behavior when client abruptly closes streams.
sara_d: I'll spike a BytesMut pool and run leak detection. If we can avoid copies into Vec<u8> on every request we should save ~6-8% CPU.
priya_k: I'll add a small experiment for canonicalizing the cache-key (lowercase + trim tokens) and run kv_hit_rate check.
alex_mason: Good — owners assigned. If we get MSG_MORE + buffer reuse + cache normalizer on canary we should be within 2% of baseline. We'll reconvene after canary results. :thumbsup:
